subject: Presign window coordination + SOC2 artifact handoff
messages:
From: Ellen Parker <ellen.parker@brightsail.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: procure@brightsail.com
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SOC2 artifacts + presign window for portal upload

Hi Rachel —

Thanks again for the quick demo yesterday. Procurement asked me to confirm the operational window you need for uploading artifacts to the portal (we'll be pushing a few large SOC2 attachments and a CSV manifest). Our S3 policy currently enforces a 7-day max presign TTL which conflicts with our internal retention cutover. Can you confirm: 1) the minimum presign TTL Redwood requires for temporary upload workflows, and 2) whether we should provide a single bulk archive vs. a manifest-driven multipart presign?

We can do the upload tonight but will need an exception if you need >7 days. Attaching the latest SOC2 report and an initial manifest for reference.

Attachments: BrightSail_SOC2_Type2_Q1_2027.pdf (PDF, 12MB), presign-manifest-20270608.csv (CSV, 5KB)

Ellie
Ellen Parker
Security & Compliance, BrightSail
ellen.parker@brightsail.com
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Parker <ellen.parker@brightsail.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC2 artifacts + presign window for portal upload

Ellen — thanks for the files and the note. Short answers up front: Redwood's presign ingestion can work with a 3-day TTL for single-shot uploads, but for manifest-driven multipart workflows we recommend 14 days to accommodate token exchange and retries across our pipeline.

A couple of clarifying asks before we request an exception from infra:
- Is the manifest referencing multiple S3 prefixes / customer buckets or a single object bundle?
- Do any of the files include encrypted logs that require KMS cross-account access?

I'll loop in Mina (security) and Jonas (platform) to confirm we don't need additional evidence steps before we accept the bundle. If BrightSail can scope the manifest to a single bucket + prefix we should be able to do a 7-day presign with a short exception for files that need multipart.

I pasted the manifest header below and a quick checklist of what we need for a clean ingest.

--- manifest preview ---
file_name,sha256,size_bytes,s3_key
BrightSail_SOC2_Type2_Q1_2027.pdf,9f2b...c4e,12500000,bright­sail/compliance/2027/q1/soc2.pdf
presign-manifest-20270608.csv,3a8c...b11,5120,bright­sail/compliance/2027/q1/manifest.csv

Checklist for portal ingest:
- Confirm target S3 bucket/prefix (single-bucket preferred)
- Indicate if KMS cross-account is required
- Provide Whistic/OneTrust profile link or ID for automated attach
- Contact for upload troubleshooting (Slack/phone)

Thanks — I'll follow up after Mina/Jonas confirm risk posture.

—Rachel
Rachel Kim
Trust & Security, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.ai
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Ellen Parker <ellen.parker@brightsail.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 13:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC2 artifacts + presign window for portal upload

Thanks Rachel. Ran a quick review of the manifest snippet — two notes from security: 
1) If the PDF contains syslog extracts or ephemeral credential listings we need a redaction plan (we can accept a redacted version now and request an escrow copy under NDA if needed).
2) For presign TTL, 14 days is fine for multipart only if BrightSail can provide a signed access policy document (we use that in the portal to tie presigned URLs to the onboarding ticket).

Jonas — can platform confirm whether our ingestion will fail if the presigned URL expires mid-upload and whether we have automatic re-presign logic for multipart flows? If not, we'll require the longer TTL or a staged upload plan.

Mina Haddad
Security Manager, Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.ai
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Ellen Parker <ellen.parker@brightsail.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC2 artifacts + presign window for portal upload

Quick platform response: our S3 presign broker currently supports re-presign for multipart flows but only if the client returns the upload id within 48 hours. For ad-hoc pushes we don't re-initiate automatically. Practical options: 
- BrightSail provides a 14-day TTL for the multipart parts OR
- We accept a single gzipped archive (single PUT) with a 7-day presign TTL and validate integrity via the manifest checksum after completion.

I'll create a short runbook and a one-click upload page that BrightSail can use tonight; Rachel, can you confirm which approach BrightSail prefers so I can provision the right presign policy?

Attachments: presign-runbook-v1.pdf (internal), presign-policy-template.txt

Jonas Weber
Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai
From: Ellen Parker <ellen.parker@brightsail.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: procure@brightsail.com, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 16:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC2 artifacts + presign window for portal upload

Thanks all — BrightSail will go with option #2: single gzipped archive to simplify the walk-through. We'll schedule the upload for tonight at 1AM PST and provide a keystore manifest and contact on standby. Can you issue the 7-day presign and send the one-click upload link to this thread?

I uploaded the Whistic profile ID to your portal: https://whistic.com/profile/brightsail/record/12478 — feel free to pull that as the attachment reference.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Ellen
Ellen Parker
Security & Compliance, BrightSail
ellen.parker@brightsail.com
